title: LIVE CONDENSATION
freshness_label: LIVE / CURRENT MODEL (derived HRRR analysis), hourly cycles
source_name: NOAA/NCEP HRRR 3 km 2 m TMP+DPT+RH analysis, hourly cycles (derived condensation-favorability index)
variable: Derived condensation-favorability index 0-100 from dew-point depression + relative humidity (no wind, no visibility inputs)
derivation: condensation = 100*(0.65*clip((2.5-S)/2.5,0,1)^0.7 + 0.35*clip((RH-60)/40,0,1)), S = TMP-DPT in C deg. Answers how close near-surface air is to saturation (dew/frost/film condensation potential). Uses no wind or visibility data, unlike fog risk; is not relative humidity or dew point itself.
what: A derived condensation-favorability index from operational HRRR temperature, dew point, and humidity analysis: where near-surface air sits closest to saturation, dew, frost, and moisture films form on boats, docks, optics, and shoreline surfaces. High values flag nights and mornings when surfaces stay wet.
field: Condensation science (surface thermodynamics and boundary-layer meteorology) studies the phase change when humid air contacts surfaces at or below the dew point. The dew-point depression (temperature minus dew point) measures the remaining cooling needed; relative humidity weights how broadly saturated the air mass is. Together they predict dew and frost formation relevant to agriculture, infrastructure, and Great Lakes marine operations.
